ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme (AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, as consolidated by the Law of 27 October 2010 and successively amended through the Law of 14 August 2023 implementing EU Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) and Directive 2015/849 (AMLD4)); Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant le Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, 'RBE'); Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 sur le registre de commerce et des sociétés et la comptabilité des entreprises (RCS Law of 19 December 2002); Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Commercial Companies Law, as amended); CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended, on central administration and internal governance obligations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (post-CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20, public access to the Luxembourg RBE register has been suspended for the general public; access is granted to national competent authorities — Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), CSSF, tax authorities, police — without restriction, and to any person demonstrating a legitimate interest, e.g., journalists or NGOs engaged in preventing money laundering and terrorist financing; the register is not fully public and not nominee-friendly in the sense that Luxembourg law mandates substantive identification and maintains a dedicated UBO register).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuts) of the SARL — executed before a Luxembourg notary; the notary performs the obligatory UBO and sanctions-name screening prior to signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (Notaire-Résident, Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Lead document executed domestically in Luxembourg — not subject to apostille; underlying foreign identity documents must be apostilled or consular-legalized in the country of origin (for China, the Hague Apostille of 7 November 2023 applies)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each shareholder, director, and beneficial owner (China-origin passport requires translation and apostille/legalization of the underlying certification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police / exit-entry administration of the country of origin (China: Ministry of Public Security Exit-Entry Administration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state (China) or consular legalization in non-Hague states; 2023 accession of China to the Apostille Convention simplifies this to apostille only

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Conduct / police clearance certificate (Casier judiciaire) from the country of current residence — mandatory for directors and managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal-record authority of the country of residence (e.g., China: Public Security Bureau / Supreme People's Procuratorate service; France: Casier Judiciaire National; Germany: Bundeszentralregister)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Central Authority of the issuing state, followed by certified French, German, or English translation executed in Luxembourg before a sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each founder (not older than 3 months, e.g., utility bill, bank statement, or notarized certificate of residence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company, credit institution, or municipal registration authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification in the country of origin, then Hague Apostille and certified translation; a residence certificate from the commune is used for EU residents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / source of funds declaration evidencing lawful origin of the SARL's minimum share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualifying credit institution (bank) where the contributing funds are held; letter addressed to the Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter must be signed and notarized/certified; apostille of the signature where the bank is located in a Hague member state; accepted only when accompanied by the UBO's bank and financial statements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Procuration) if a founder does not personally appear before the Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of the founder's residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the POA by the competent ministry of the issuing state, with a certified French or German translation; the original POA is filed in the Luxembourg notary's records

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Curriculum Vitae of directors and managers (customary professional substance evidence filed in the AML/KYC file)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The individual director/manager, signature notarized in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Optional notarization and apostille; accepted with certified translation into French or English; validity until lapse of facts

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and documented screening of all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against (i) the Luxembourg national freezing list maintained by the Ministry of Finance, (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (iii) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list (EU Reg. 269/2014, etc.), (iv) the OFAC SDN list as prudent practice given USD-based payment rails (Wise B2B, Payoneer), and (v) the Luxembourg Politically Exposed Persons framework defined in Article 3 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, including domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates; enhanced due diligence (EDD) and beneficial-ownership-piercing measures are mandatory for any PEP or high-risk jurisdiction source of funds; the notary and the designated AML compliance officer of the corporate service provider must document the screening in the statutory AML/CFT file (dossier de lutte anti-blanchiment) before incorporation proceeds; and the Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier, 'CRF') requires all professionals to report any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing; risk classification for this multilingual localization agency is Low_Risk_Standard (ISIC 7490), yet the complete CDD-KYC checklist remains non-waivable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — https://www.lbr.lu, operated jointly by the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE); name availability search is conducted in real time via the LBR's 'Recherche' portal and cross-checked by the drafting notary before execution of the Statutes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official legal corporate name of a Luxembourg SARL must be expressed in one of the three official administrative languages of Luxembourg — French, German, or Luxembourgish — or, in recognized practice, in a Latin-script romanized form of a foreign language; Luxembourgish/French predominance is customary. Non-Latin script is not accepted in the RCS registration field; any commercial name material in Chinese characters must be accompanied by a certified French, German, or English transliteration/translation deposited with the notary. The corporate name must be distinctive, must not be contrary to public order or bonnes mœurs, must not mislead the public, and must include a legal-form indication that accurately reflects the SARL status (e.g., 'SARL' or 'S.à r.l.'); suffixes such as 'SA', 'SCS', 'SCA' are prohibited when not accurate. The doctrine of 'company name availability' requires that the name not be identical or confusingly similar to any name already appearing in the RCS, nor to any mark protected by the Luxembourg or EU trademark registries (Luxembourg Intellectual Property Office — INPI Luxembourg; EUIPO Alicante).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Credit or any expression implying banking or deposit-taking activity
Assurance / Assurances / Reassurance — reserved to regulated insurance undertakings
Fonds d'investissement / OPC / SICAV / SICAR / FCP — reserved to regulated collective investment vehicles
Fiduciaire / Trust / Trusteeship — restricted to licensed professionals
Réviseur d'entreprises / Auditeur / Audit / Experts-comptables — restricted to certified public accounting professionals
Bourse / Stock Exchange — reserved for regulated market operators
Université / École / Enseignement supérieur — reserved to recognized educational institutions
Luxembourg / Luxembourgish and its cognates — implies state sponsorship and requires prior authorization
Ministère / Administration / Gouvernement / État — implies public authority or government affiliation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a statutory name-reservation system independent of the incorporation notarial act; name availability is verified at the moment of drafting, and the notary secures the name through the rectification and deposit mechanism at the RCS upon execution of the statutes. If the chosen name is rejected by the RCS — whether because of identity/confusion with an existing registration, misleading character, or use of a protected token — the following standard operating procedure applies: (1) The notary must be informed in writing by the RCS within one month of registration request; (2) The applicant submits two (2) alternative names in order of preference, with the notary performing a fresh LBR availability search for each; (3) The notary files a new registration request with the corrected name and pays the applicable re-filing fee (EUR 15–35, depending on the corrected entry); (4) If the rejection is contested, the applicant files an administrative appeal with the Ministre de la Justice (Ministry of Justice) within 3 months of notification, accompanied by legal argument proving distinctiveness and absence of confusion (Art. 14, Law of 19 December 2002); (5) If the ministerial decision is negative, a judicial appeal lies to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (District Court) sitting in commercial matters, with a 3-month prescription period, and the procedural timeline normally finalizes within 2–4 months; throughout the appeal, the draft articles of association are held in escrow with the notary and no commercial operation or signature of statutes occurs until the name is cleared.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with substantive limitations. Luxembourg law (Art. 710-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended; RBE Law of 13 January 2019; CSSF Reg. 12-02) requires a genuine registered office different from the statutorily declared administrative seat, and the tax administration (Administration des contributions directes, 'ACD') applies the real-activity test to avoid deemed-residence deviations. For a low-risk professional translation and dubbing agency with no regulated license, a serviced-office or 'domiciliation' arrangement — where a licensed corporate domiciliation agent provides a physical Luxembourg address, mail handling, and meeting facilities — is widely accepted and constitutes current market practice (LBR-registered domiciliation agents are regulated by the Ministry of Justice under Article 27 of the Law of 19 December 2002). However, a pure virtual mailbox with no local decision-making, no local management, no local bank account engagement, and no documentary evidence of substance in Luxembourg would expose the SARL to: (i) reclassification of its tax residence abroad, (ii) denial of Luxembourg VAT registration, and (iii) potential criminal-liability exposure of the managers for fictive registered office. Recommended practice: a serviced office in Luxembourg City with at least one Luxembourg-resident director or an executive manager domiciled in Luxembourg; the localization agency's project-management and invoicing functions may legitimately be performed remotely, but the SARL's statutory minutes, accounting records, and VAT filing obligations must be materially anchored in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Moderate, quantified at approximately 10% per annum in the first three years of operation for an unlicensed, low-risk service company. The RCS does not conduct routine physical inspections of the registered office; nevertheless, (i) the ACD may perform unannounced on-site inspections in connection with VAT refund audits or transfer-pricing substance reviews, (ii) the CCSS (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale) annually inspects employers, but the SARL with no Luxembourg employees reduces this likelihood, and (iii) the police judiciaire and the CRF can visit the premises for AML/CFT investigations, though this probability is below 5% absent suspicious activity indicators. The domiciliation agent must maintain a physical office with signage and administrative archives; an agency that demonstrates mere post-box presence will raise the inspection likelihood to 35%–45%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory notarial tariff for capital constitution of a SARL (approximately EUR 1,500–2,500 for a EUR 12,000 share capital, depending on number of shareholders and annexes; statutory 'droit d'acte' plus disbursements)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS corporate registration fee — entry of the SARL in the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (Filing A: 'Constitution de société')
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (Luxembourg Business Registers)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff pursuant to Article 34 of the Law of 19 December 2002 (EUR 75–150 depending on the filing channel; standard electronic filing fee EUR 86)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation in the official electronic legal gazette (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, 'RESA')

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille fee per document (China: approximately USD 10–35 per document); certified translation and administrative handling add USD 150–300; total estimated for a 4-document bundle

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 710-1 to 710-25 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Law of 19 December 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Business Registers; Civil Code Title XV, Articles 1832 et seq. as applicable
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 15-7a, Boulevard de la Foire, L-1528 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) together with the authenticated articles of association (statuts coordonnés), filed electronically with the Luxembourg Business Registers
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL requires a minimum issued share capital of EUR 12,000 (approximately USD 13,000), fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked account at a Luxembourg bank in the name of the company in formation and released only upon RCS registration; contributions in kind require a statutory auditor's valuation report and effective transfer of the asset to the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators having subscribed and fully paid the share capital of EUR 12,000, adopt the notarized articles of association as the governance charter of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the address in the Articles and that the manager shall notify the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed manager (gérant) with sole authority to bind the Company, execute filings, contracts and tax registrations. RESOLVED, that the bank blockage certificate is accepted, the capital shall be released upon RCS registration, and the manager shall complete VAT and social security enrolment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – online name clearance service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit electronically through the My-LBR portal requesting a certificate of non-confusion for the proposed SARL name. The RCS verifies the uniqueness of the distinctive element and compatibility with the SARL legal form. Upon clearance, retain the reference number for inclusion in the notarial deed; the certificate is valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Request form signed by the incorporator
Passport copy of each incorporator and intended manager
Statement of proposed activity (ISIC 7490 multilingual localization services)
Registered office address if known
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or objected, examine the RCS notice, request an administrative review or submit a new name variant; resubmission is permitted without loss of priority if done within the response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete a bank client onboarding form for the company-in-formation and deposit the full subscription amount (minimum EUR 12,000) on a blocked account designated 'SARL en formation'. Obtain the bank's irrevocable certificate of blockage confirming the identity and amount. Deliver the original certificate to the notary at closing.
required_dossiers: Bank account application in the proposed company name
Draft articles of association
Passport or identity documents of shareholders and manager
Beneficial owner identification and source-of-funds declaration
Reference to the RCS name clearance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional economic rationale, provide the localization-agency business plan and source-of-wealth documents; if refusal persists, release the funds without penalty and submit a substitute certificate from another bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public notary in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (Cercle des Notaires)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present to the notary the proposed articles, RCS name certificate, original bank blockage certificate, and identity documents. The notary authenticates the deed, verifies legal capacity and full subscription/payment, and records the appointment of the manager. The notary delivers an expédition and transmits the deed to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Original bank blockage certificate
RCS name clearance reference
Draft articles signed by all shareholders
Passports or residence permits of shareholders and manager
Declaration of acceptance of office by the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects, amend the draft articles and execute an addendum; any third-party observations must be resolved before re-signature. A pre-filing avis préalable may be sought from the RCS to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and publication at the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS file electronically or at the RCS counters, including the notarial deed and confirmation of registered office. The RCS verifies name, legal form, and legality, registers the SARL, and forwards the abstract for publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). Upon admission obtain the RCS registration number and official legal extract.
required_dossiers: Authentic notarial copy of the incorporation deed
Completed registration form signed by the manager
Proof of registered office (lease or ownership title)
Declaration of good repute and specimen signature of the manager
Copy of RCS name clearance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, respond by formal note within the stated deadline; if a legal amendment is required, execute a notarial addendum and resubmit. First corrections filed within 10 business days are not subject to a second publication fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, social security and establishment registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale de la PME
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a declaration of commencement of activity with the AEDT for VAT purposes and obtain a Luxembourg VAT number. Register with the ACD for corporate income tax and municipal business tax. Enroll as an employer with the CCSS. If the activity is considered commercial under the establishment law, apply for the general authorization (autorisation d'établissement) with the Ministry of the Economy; ISIC 7490 translation services carry no sectoral qualification requirement.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract and notarial deed
Identification of manager and beneficial owners
Lease contract or proof of registered office
Business activity description and projected turnover
Manager's police record or declaration of good repute
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT or CCSS query missing data, correct and resubmit within 5 business days. If the establishment authorization is refused, an appeal lies to the Minister of the Economy under the Administrative Procedure Code within 3 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance and internal bookkeeping formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office / management of the company; Luxembourg Business Registers – beneficial ownership register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the inaugural general shareholders' meeting or adopt a written resolution confirming the share subscription, appointment of the manager, registered office adoption, and governance charter. Open the share register (registre des parts). File the beneficial ownership declaration with the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners, and appoint an independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) if statutory thresholds are met. Prepare the opening balance sheet and establish accounting records.
required_dossiers: Signed first shareholders'/board resolution
Share register and list of shareholders
Beneficial ownership register form
Manager appointment acceptance
Opening balance sheet and accounting system set-up documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership declaration is rejected, verify identification data and resubmit through the e-justice platform; first late or corrected filings are accepted without penalty when made within 30 days of initial registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — office-based professional services under ISIC 7490; no industrial licensing board intervenes. General commercial registration remains with the Luxembourg Business Registers and, if applicable, establishment authorization from the Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale de la PME.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating license required for multilingual translation, localization and media dubbing services (non-regulated activity).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA required; the activity involves only administrative office operations and does not constitute an Annex I or Annex II installation under the law of 6 September 2007 on integrated environmental approach.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges or VOC/solvent emissions are anticipated. The entity must nevertheless comply with municipal wastewater discharge rules and waste separation obligations under the law of 21 March 2017. Any dubbing studio equipment must meet occupational noise limits under the Labor Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for office premises under the Grand-Duchy Fire and Rescue Service (CGDIS); structural load certificate from the landlord or a registered engineer for heavy studio or acoustic equipment; workplace health and safety clearance under the Labor Code; electrical installation verification for recording and dubbing equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); central e-portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL obtains its national registration number (matricule) automatically upon incorporation through the Luxembourg Business Registers. For VAT, the SARL must submit Form 1 to the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu within 15 days of commencing taxable activity; non-resident entities without an establishment in Luxembourg must register when making taxable supplies in Luxembourg or when distance sales to Luxembourg consumers exceed the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box election. The SARL is irrebuttably treated as a taxable corporate entity. ATAD hybrid mismatch rules apply to neutralize mismatch outcomes. Elective regimes include: VAT group registration as a single taxable person (Article 61 of the VAT Law), option to tax the letting of immovable property (Article 44(2)), and election to benefit from the participation exemption (75% dividend deduction and full capital gains exemption) for qualifying shareholdings.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Luxembourg-established taxable persons have no mandatory registration below an annual taxable turnover of EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT). A non-established supplier is required to register for Luxembourg VAT if it makes taxable supplies of goods or services in Luxembourg and the reverse charge is unavailable, or if its distance sales to Luxembourg consumers exceed the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold (formerly EUR 100,000 before 1 July 2021).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping requirement, or mandatory continuous transaction control. E-invoicing is permissible and accepted, VAT returns must be filed electronically via the eCDF channel (monthly/quarterly), and B2G invoicing functions through the PEPPOL infrastructure on an optional basis.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of tangible goods outside the EU qualifies for zero-rating where goods leave Luxembourg unmodified, export is evidenced within 90 days, and legal ownership has transferred to a non-EU purchaser. Intra-community supplies (ICS) are zero-rated where the customer supplies a valid EU VAT number and the transaction is listed in the EC Sales List. Services provided to non-EU business customers are generally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction). Services performed for a non-EU private customer (e.g., multilingual localization) are zero-rated if the effective use and enjoyment of the service is outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document) and/or electronic proof of exit
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR or other transport document evidencing physical departure from Luxembourg
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT confirmation demonstrating foreign exchange repatriation
Commercial invoice and export contract or client purchase order
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where export zero-rating is applied without the required documentary evidence, Luxembourg VAT authorities may assess the VAT not paid, charge interest at the statutory rate, and impose administrative fines of 10% to 100% of the tax deficiency depending on the degree of negligence. Intentional fraud triggers criminal penalties under Article 58 of the VAT Law, including imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and/or fines up to EUR 50,000, plus a five-year retrospective clawback period (10 years in case of proven fraud).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), the National Central Bank of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and a member of the Eurosystem; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the competent supervisory authority for credit institutions, payment institutions and e-money institutions under the amended AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02. The European Central Bank (ECB) holds ultimate monetary and euro-liquidity authority via T2/TARGET Services. Luxembourg directly applies the EU Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR), Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD), and Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility: the euro is freely convertible and Luxembourg maintains no exchange-control body, no prior-approval mechanism and no quantitative limits on current or capital transactions. Article 63(1) TFEU prohibits all restrictions on the movement of capital and payments between Member States and third countries. A Luxembourg SARL may invoice foreign clients, hold foreign-currency accounts, convert EUR into any currency, and repatriate profits without BCL or CSSF consent. Profit-remittance hurdles are fiscal rather than currency-related: (i) Luxembourg dividend withholding tax of 15% (reducible to 0% under the EU Parent–Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for 12 months, or under an applicable tax treaty); (ii) the commercial-company net-assets distributability test (Article 111 of the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended) requiring an approved balance sheet and, where reserves are distributed, a statutory auditor's certification; and (iii) for larger remittances, banks may request evidence of current corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax filings. No BCL authorization, economic-substance visa, or exchange quotation is required for ordinary treasury activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender ratio, no repatriation deadline, and no mandatory conversion of export or service proceeds for resident enterprises. A SARL engaged in professional multilingual translation and media dubbing (ISIC 7490) may retain all export receipts in foreign currency in any EU-resident bank account. The only associated obligation is statistical: BCL and STATEC balance-of-payments surveys may require resident service exporters to report invoice-level proceeds on a quarterly or annual basis, purely for compilation of national accounts. This reporting is ex-post, non-restrictive, and has no liquidity-management or conversion consequence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (blocked constitution deposit) / Operational Current Account; multi-currency USD, GBP and JPY sub-accounts
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account; corporate e-banking with SEPA and SWIFT gpi connectivity
Operational Account with EUR and USD cash-pool; accommodates non-resident directors through Luxembourg-licensed KYC
Operational Account; fully digital SME onboarding, SEPA Instant and MT103 execution
Operational Account; relationship-led mid-market treasury and FX services
Operational Account; private-banking product focus with fee structure mismatched for a low-risk professional-services entity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for disbursement-only usage. Wise Europe SA (e-money institution licensed by the National Bank of Belgium and passported into Luxembourg under PSD2/E-Money Directive) and Payoneer (EU payment-/e-money-licensed passporting) are viable for low- to mid-value B2B contractor payouts and multi-currency conversions for a localization agency. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI cannot issue the bank attestation (certificat de dépôt) required by the notary for the €12,000 SARL registered capital; that capital must be deposited and blocked at a Luxembourg credit institution; (ii) Regulation (EU) 2015/847 fund-transfer information and CSSF AML duties apply identically, so the EMI will require the same UBO and source-of-funds evidence at onboarding; (iii) tier-1 banks do not treat EMI balances as reference liquidity for credit assessment; and (iv) EMI sanctions filters are less configurable than correspondent-bank filters, so high-value flows to sensitive jurisdictions should remain on SWIFT MT103. Routing rule: tier-1 bank for statutory capital, client receipts, tax payments and balances above US$ 100,000; Wise B2B/Payoneer for recurring vendor and freelancer payouts below that threshold.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is accepted by most Luxembourg credit institutions for a standard, low-risk SARL providing professional services, subject to: (i) a live video-identification interview of each director and UBO, performed by the bank or a CSSF-approved video-KYC provider under the amended AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Circular 19/740; (ii) an eIDAS-qualified electronic signature on the account agreement; and (iii) certified passport copies, proof of residential address, and the RCS excerpt of the SARL. Banks retain discretionary power to require physical attendance at a Luxembourg office or branch where the UBO chain includes non-EEA intermediate companies, where directors are tax-resident in jurisdictions without effective CRS/AEOI exchange, or where projected counterparty flows touch sanctioned states. For non-EU directors delegating signature to a Luxembourg agent, a notarized power of attorney and a physical interview of the authorized agent are standard. In all cases, at least one natural-person signatory must be identified and verified; fully anonymous account opening is prohibited.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity and CRS mismatch: shareholders are routed through an offshore holding structure, trust or foundation without economic explanation, delaying RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) registration and creating correspondent-bank refusal risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal-structure chart with control percentages; RBE filing receipt for the SARL; CRS tax-residence self-certifications (Form CRC) of every natural-person UBO; notarized or certified passport copies and recent proof of residential address; FATCA/CRS declarations filed with the Luxembourg direct tax administration (AED); constitutive documents and registry excerpts of all intermediate holding vehicles; and a source-of-wealth memorandum supported by personal tax returns or audited financial statements of each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Untraceable source of the €12,000 registered capital: third-party funding, cash deposits, or rapid chain transfers without a documentary chain of funds, creating a false-positive money-laundering flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of incorporation with a bank attestation (certificat de dépôt) issued by a Luxembourg credit institution; six months of bank statements of the contributing shareholder evidencing legally accumulated funds; shareholder resolution authorizing the subscription and payment; SEPA/SEPA Instant or SWIFT MT103 credit referencing the RCS file number and ISO purpose code 'CAPC' or 'INVE'; where the contributor is a company, its UBO declaration, registry excerpt, and audited financial statements for the last fiscal year.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payout red flags: recurring vendor payments via Wise B2B/Payoneer to emerging-market dubbing studios or subtitling suppliers in high-risk jurisdictions, high refund rates, or rapid pass-through transactions resembling layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed localization master service agreements and per-project purchase orders; EU consolidated financial sanctions screening results for each counterparty and jurisdiction; declarations of beneficial ownership and bank-account confirmation from each vendor; complete invoice packages with VAT and OSS references; client and vendor onboarding questionnaires capturing physical address, industry, and beneficial owners; and a written treasury policy restricting sanctioned jurisdictions and setting escalation thresholds for refunds and round-trip transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance mismatch: declared activity (ISIC 7490 professional multilingual translation and media dubbing) produces a bank narrative dominated by large technology-platform receipts, intercompany round-trips, or payments inconsistent with per-asset revenue models.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Auditable delivery evidence (translation-memory data, subtitle and dubbing asset manifests, media licensing contracts); a business plan with per-word/per-asset pricing reconciling to projected turnover; client reference letters and purchase agreements; Luxembourg annual accounts and VAT returns (including OSS declarations where relevant) proving operational substance; transfer pricing documentation for intercompany or shareholder management fees; and staffing and infrastructure records (office lease, payroll, subcontractor agreements) consistent with the declared localization activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Control nexus concern: all directors or ultimate decision-makers resident outside the EEA, raising 'director-in-absentia' issues and uncertainty regarding who actually exercises management during AML and fraud reviews.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized or legalized board resolutions appointing a Luxembourg-domiciled manager or authorized signatory; an executed management agreement with a Luxembourg service provider; substance evidence (registered-office lease, employee payroll, central-administration records); criminal-record certificates of each director from their country of residence; a declaration of ultimate control validated by a Luxembourg law firm opinion; and minutes of periodic in-person or video board meetings demonstrating active exercise of management.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The €12,000 registered capital of a Luxembourg SARL must be fully paid in cash, subscribed and deposited before incorporation. Procedure: the notary instructs the chosen Luxembourg credit institution to open a blocked capital account (compte bloqué/séquestre) in the name of the future SARL; the shareholder executes a SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst, settled in approximately ten seconds via TIPS/T2) if the remitter holds an EEA bank account, or a SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA remitters, with remittance text referencing the notary file and the future RCS number. After the notarial deed is passed and RCS registration obtained, the blocked balance converts automatically to the operational current account. Additional equity contributions (share premium, capital increase, super dividend re-injection) arrive by SEPA SCT/SCT Inst or MT103 using ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPC' (capital contribution) or 'CINV' (capital investment); shareholder loans use 'LITI'. The receiving bank must verify complete remitter and beneficiary information under Regulation (EU) 2015/847; any capital flow at or above EUR 10,000 triggers enhanced due diligence requiring the underlying notarial deed, shareholder resolution, and source-of-funds evidence. No BCL authorization or FX license is required for inbound capital; USD-denominated equity contributions are cleared via SWIFT gpi correspondent channels and pass through the bank's OFAC/EU sanctions filters with purpose code 'CAPC' restated for regulatory consistency.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Eurozone and EEA disbursements: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) via TARGET2/STEP2/TIPS, settled T+0 with no correspondent deduction, using the vendor's IBAN and the service invoice reference. Non-EEA and non-EUR disbursements: SWIFT MT103 with SWIFT gpi tracking through the Luxembourg bank's correspondent network — USD via a U.S. clearing agent (Fedwire/CHIPS), GBP via CHAPS or Faster Payments, and JPY via BOJ-NET. For high-value licensing or media-rights acquisitions above EUR 100,000 where trade-settlement security is required, a commercial documentary letter of credit (advised or confirmed by the Luxembourg bank, payable at sight under UCP 600) or a documentary clean collection is permissible. For recurring mid-value contractor payouts between US$ 5,000 and US$ 50,000, Wise B2B and Payoneer multi-currency virtual accounts provide local clearing in more than 40 markets at lower cost; however, treasury policy should escalate any single vendor payout above US$ 100,000 to a direct MT103 to preserve a clean audit trail. All outbound payment narratives must state the service contract reference and the applicable VAT treatment (reverse charge or OSS), with monthly reconciliation to the SARL's Luxembourg VAT returns.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY) for firm localization and dubbing receivables/payables, executed under a 2002 ISDA Master Agreement with an EU/EEA credit institution; non-financial counterparty hedge-only trades are exempt from mandatory clearing under EMIR Refit thresholds, and no BCL or CSSF license is required for treasury end-user hedging.

FX swap agreements combining a spot leg and a forward leg, used to roll or rotate existing hedge maturities and to manage timing mismatches in licensing cash flows; same ISDA and EMIR treatment as outright forwards, with settlement within two business days exempt from uncleared margin rules.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for material intercompany or media-rights financing with tenor above 12 months, subject to EMIR trade-repository reporting, daily variation-margin arrangements with EU counterparties, and IFRS 9 hedge documentation evidencing hedge-only intent.

Plain-vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/JPY FX options (ATMF calls and puts, zero-premium collars) to hedge contingent tender exposure for multilingual media localization contracts, with premium sizes constrained by a board-approved hedging policy and paid in EUR from the operational account.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in euros against restricted-currency exposures (CNY, INR, NGN, BRL, TRY) arising from emerging-market vendor payments to dubbing studios and subtitling suppliers, settled in EUR; the bank executes under an ISDA NDF confirmation and requires the underlying USD- or EUR-denominated vendor invoices to validate the hedge-only purpose.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, annex) filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval and no later than 7 months after the financial year-end; calendar-year companies must approve accounts at the AGM within 6 months of the balance sheet date (deadline: 31 July for 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SARL to a judicial order on the request of the Public Prosecutor carrying an 'astreinte' (coercive daily fine); failure for three consecutive years can lead to court-ordered compulsory dissolution and administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner (UBO) data in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every 12 months from the most recent RBE confirmation or registration; the annual confirmation must be submitted before the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm UBO details is a criminal offence punishable by fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to 12 months; administrative fines may also be imposed for incomplete or false information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur la fortune, IF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Bureau d'imposition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed in accordance with the ACD corporate tax return schedule, generally by 31 May of the assessment year for calendar-year taxpayers; extensions may be granted by the tax office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or omission leads to 'taxation d'office' (provisional assessment) and default interest of 0.87% per month on unpaid tax; late-filing penalties may reach 10% of the assessed net wealth tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an approved statutory auditor when it exceeds two of three criteria for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million, net turnover > EUR 8.8 million, average headcount > 50. Below these thresholds, the SARL is exempt from mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial and annual accounts (implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must annually confirm the accuracy of its beneficial-ownership information in the RBE electronic register at least once every 12 months; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with the RBE within one month of the change, after which the annual confirmation cycle resets.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des associés / sociétaires)
Minute book of shareholders' meetings and decisions (procès-verbaux des assemblées et des décisions des associés)
Register of managers' (gérants') decisions and attendance records

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax, solidarity surcharge, and municipal business tax for Luxembourg City; base IRC is 17% on first €175,000 and 15% above)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (8% for new tangible assets, 12% for certain intangible assets), participation exemption for qualifying shareholdings, and notional interest deduction on new equity capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 500/MT (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; extension to 31 December may be granted upon justified request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the company (name, registered office, RCS number, tax ID)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax ID and RCS number; non-resident directors must be identified with foreign tax IDs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net profit before tax adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income if tax resident; non-resident companies only report Luxembourg-source income.
Only expenses directly related to Luxembourg-source income are deductible for non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (foreign tax credit, investment tax credit, IP box deduction)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim treaty relief or unilateral foreign tax credit for taxes paid on Luxembourg-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income and calculation of corporate income tax (IRC) and solidarity surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply progressive rates: 17% on first €175,000, 15% on excess; add 7% solidarity surcharge on IRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax (Communal Trade Tax) calculation based on taxable income and municipal multiplier
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a permanent establishment in Luxembourg are subject to municipal business tax on income attributable to that PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of €10 per day (max €1,000) plus 0.6% per month of unpaid tax (max 10%). Interest on late payment at 0.8% per month. Criminal sanctions for intentional non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥10% for 12 months; treaty rates may apply)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence state, complete Form 500 (withholding tax exemption request) via MyTaxichet.lu, and provide evidence of beneficial ownership. The Luxembourg tax administration issues a clearance certificate for reduced WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and interest is 0% (no withholding tax on outbound payments). Treaty rates may apply for inbound payments, but Luxembourg does not impose WHT on outbound royalties/interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 (group consolidated revenue) and EUR 1,000,000 (related party transactions) trigger mandatory Local File and Master File preparation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) primarily to pure holding, financing, and IP companies. For a translation/localization agency, substance is presumed if it has adequate premises, employees, and operational activity. However, the company must avoid being classified as a shell entity under EU anti-abuse rules (ATAD) and Luxembourg's general anti-abuse rule (GAAR).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false invoicing, or concealment of taxable transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; additional tax penalties up to 100% of evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for civil restitution of evaded taxes, subject to travel bans and asset freezes; criminal prosecution may lead to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without real business activity, no employees, no physical office, or acting as a conduit for tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, and imposition of 15% WHT on deemed dividends; penalties up to €50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for unpaid taxes and subject to disqualification from serving as directors in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining adequate records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1,000,000 for legal entities; suspension of business license; criminal sanctions for responsible individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined up to €250,000 and imprisoned up to 5 years for willful AML violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation, or applying non-arm's length pricing in related party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties up to 10% of the adjustment, and interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing.
